extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners; patent applicants and their attorneys interacting with KIPO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive instructions for handling extensions, amendments, written arguments, document requests, searches, interviews, delivery, and decisions during patent examination at KIPO. Targets examiners' decision-making and applicants' procedural compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension request approval and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an extension request does not exceed four months and the concerned fee has been paid, the request for period extension is deemed to have been approved upon filing. For a request for four-month extension, a forewarning of 'no further extension will be approved afterward' attached to the written approval shall be notified of an applicant. If an applicant makes another extension request afterwards, it shall be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees shall be refunded where a request for period extension is rejected. For overdue extension requests of the formality-examination period (or extended period), an examiner shall provide an opportunity for petition to an applicant and return the request form and refund the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of designated period by request
rubrics_metrics.description: The period for a patent-related procedure having been designated can be reduced according to a request. Where a request for period reduction is made or where a written amendment or description stipulating the purport to reduce the designated period is submitted, the designated period is deemed to have been expired as of the submission date of a reduction request form or a written amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension for trial request (trial against rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person can request to extend the period for requesting for a trial against to reject a patent (a utility model) application only for once and for up to 30 days. However, the number and the period of extension may be further extended for a person residing in an area that is difficult to access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such request is made, the President of IPT (Trial Policy Division) shall review the requirements and determine whether it is approved or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late submission of specification/drawings returned; formal amendments allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the written amendment for specification or drawing(s) is submitted after the designated period, it shall be returned by reason of overdue submission. However, an amendment of application as to formalities shall be admitted anytime before invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of written arguments (with or without amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a written argument is submitted along with an amendment, an examiner shall review both the argument and the amendment in depth and determine as to whether the notified grounds for rejection can be overcome or not. Also, where only a written argument is submitted without an amendment, an examiner shall consider sufficiently an argument to determine as to the notified grounds for rejection can be overcome or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written argument or other documents including experiment results in response to the notification of the grounds for rejection shall not be a part of the specification. However, as these documents are submitted to clarify or verify matters in the detailed description, an examiner may refer to them to decide patentability. If an applicant insists matters to be amended in a written argument but fails to submit an amendment, the examination shall be made on the detailed description and claims as notified; where insisted amendments and actual amendments differ, examination is based on the actual amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final specification determination after multiple amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The final specification to be examined shall be determined automatically through the Patent Net after reflecting amendment to the detailed description, claims and drawings. An amendment to the full text of the specification shall be replaced as the final specification to be examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple written amendments are submitted, the final specification is determined as a combination of the most recent (final) amended elements per part (detailed description, each claim, drawings). Example provided showing how 1st and 2nd amendments combine per-element to form the 2nd amended specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of amendments under Article 52(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment in response the final ground for rejection or made upon the request for reexamination is dismissed pursuant to the Article 52(1) of the Patent Act, an examiner considers the amendment deemed to have never been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section '11. Amendment in Response to Final Notification of Ground for Rejection' for referral and handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of self-amendments and non-final-response amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A self-amendment submitted before examination starts and an amendment in response to the non-final notification of grounds for rejection within the period (designated for submission of a written argument) are recognized as submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules for amendments sent before applicant receives notification
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may self-amend during the period between the delivery of the ground for rejection by an examiner and its receipt by an applicant. To expedite proceedings, where an applicant submits an amendment during the period between an examiner's sending of the grounds for rejection and an applicant's receiving of it, the amendment is regarded as being submitted earlier than receiving the ground for rejection if a date of applicant's receipt can be confirmed by special mail registered receipt, unless evidence shows notification delivery precedes amendment submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a written amendment identifies a delivery number of a notification for rejection ground, the notification delivery is regarded to be earlier than amendment submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination outcomes after amendments (general rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner re-examines an amended specification: (a) if no ground for rejection is discovered, grant a patent; (b) if a previously notified ground remains, reject the application; (c) if notified grounds are overcome but a new ground is generated by the amendment or previously existing but unnotified grounds are discovered, notify the non-final ground(s) again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules apply whether one amendment or multiple amendments are submitted; additional clause: where an amendment generates a ground due to Amendment b, an examiner may notify final ground for rejection in certain cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request and use of documents/samples for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If considered necessary to expedite examination, an examiner may ask an applicant to submit documents and other reference materials required for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested documents include: related documents and translations for international applications and other offices' outcomes; a claim-to-description mapping by paragraph; a statement explaining relations among claims for voluminous applications; a written summary/gist when subject matter is too complex; samples or experimental results where effects cannot be verified otherwise (to confirm sufficiency); statements explaining derivation of formulas, definitions and meanings of technical terms; clarification of applicants' claims in arguments when hard to understand. Requests must be specific, made under examiner's name, and fall within the period for submission of written arguments. Documents are only reference material and cannot substitute or supplement the specification. Examiners must keep lists, store and return documents with care; if applicant fails to respond, examiner shall not invalidate the application procedure. Evidential documents that are periodicals or published copies may be used as prior art without further evidence; other documents may be used as prior art only if the examiner is confident of the facts without further evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for applications invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or finally decided by examiner, anyone can provide relevant evidence to an examiner to argue that an application should not be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information provision can be made by any person or corporation (incompetent minors must appoint legal representative). Examiner may refer to documents/information provided by a group or association instead of invalidating/returning them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triggers for additional search during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: During examination, an examiner shall conduct additional searches where: (i) a written argument, personal interview, or third-party information reveals incomplete understanding leading to incomplete search; (ii) amended claims include subject matter not covered by the original search; (iii) examiner intends to examine inventions excluded previously due to lack of unity of invention; (iv) an international patent application enters the domestic stage and translation is expected; (v) other cases deemed necessary for additional research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and process for examination deferral or extension of processing period
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may defer an examination or extend the processing period within 2 months when an application falls under specified cases, including: earlier/conflicting applications not laid open or lacking request for examination; period during which an earlier priority application is deemed withdrawn has not elapsed; related patent trial or proceeding pending; need to outsource prior art search or obtain expert opinion; period for submission of evidential documents for priority right not elapsed; or other necessary occasions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferral/extension must be reported to the head of the Examination Unit and notified to the applicant. Examiner shall review more than once a month to confirm whether reasons have been resolved and terminate deferral/extension when cleared. Further deferral/extensions require reporting up chain and applicant notification; specific reasons must be notified when re-deciding to defer/extend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document delivery principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents shall be sent by registered mail except where the party or attorney receives in person or uses information network. The registration receipt shall be kept. Documents shall be delivered to a legitimate receiver (attorney if appointed, sub-attorney, or the party), with rules on priority where multiple agencies or multiple attorneys exist. Change of delivery address must be reported without delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If delivery fails due to unjustified rejection by receiver, the date of sending is regarded as the receiving date. See Part 1 General Rules for more details. Special delivery methods apply for trial rulings or written decisions per postal laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery by public notification when address unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: When documents cannot be delivered because the residential or business address of the addressee is unclear (cannot be verified even using the Resident Registration Use System), documents shall be delivered by public notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: (i) file facts about returned documents and communicate to examiner; examiner verifies address by telephone and may resend with a guide to report information change; (ii) where Resident Registration Use System address matches telephone-confirmed address, deliver by public notification; (iii) if resend to Resident Registration address and returned again, deliver by public notification with no further confirmation. For corporations Resident Registration Use System cannot be used; examiner must make maximal efforts and send to legal address at least once before public notification. Examiners may adopt different delivery methods if case-by-case review identifies a reliable method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal interview as ancillary examination method
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant or attorney requests or an examiner considers necessary for a prompt and fair examination, an examiner may have a personal interview with the party as ancillary method. Cases include comparative explanation between claimed invention and prior art, clarification of grounds for rejection, need to explain written argument, complicated subject matter, or other recognized needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests may be made by fax, telephone, email, information network or written application; one request per application (exceptions when same examiner handles multiple applications). Interviews can be face-to-face, video phone, or other designated facilities. Examiner should review documents in advance, may request reference documents beforehand, confirm legitimacy of participants, require proxies where delegation is limited, allow participant accompaniment by inventor or related person, and keep a signed interview log including participants, contents and results. Interviews are generally one per application (up to two if necessary). Agreements from interviews must be executed promptly and an interview shall not be the basis to simplify or omit requisite statements in notifications/decisions. If examiner discovers new grounds after an interview and intends to act contrary to interview outcome, the examiner shall communicate that purport and continue examination. Examiner may request materials presented at interview; if interview held within written-argument period, participants must submit agreed documents by that period; choosing to respond differently requires notifying examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for personal interview on visit
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request an examiner to visit for communication (personal interview on visit). Examiner contacts by telephone to determine need; visit allowed only if telephone communication is difficult or necessary for prompt/accurate examination. In principle carried out in a Regional Intellectual Property Center, but other places allowed under mutual agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When changing date or keeping log for an on-visit interview, examiner shall comply with the general personal interview procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admitting or dismissing amendments in response to final notification of grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike non-final notifications, when receiving an amendment in response to the final grounds for rejection, an examiner shall determine whether to dismiss the amendment before assessing patentability. If issuance of the final notification is inappropriate, the examiner shall admit the amendment. Where the final grounds are appropriate and amendment fails to meet amendment scope under Article 47(2) and (3) or generates new grounds for rejection (except certain deletions), the amendment shall be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no amendment is made or amendment limited to response to final notification (e.g., just reducing claim) and final notification was inappropriate (should have been non-final), the examiner shall notify grounds again instead of rejecting. If applicant treats a final as non-final and submits amendments as non-final, examiner may decide to reject. When multiple amendments are submitted within the written-argument period, examiner determines admission in reverse order of submission. Examples (Ex1–Ex5) illustrate what constitutes a 'new ground for rejection' generated by amendment and cases where deletions are admitted despite causing downstream deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and handling of 'new ground for rejection' from amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'new ground for rejection' refers to where submission of the amendment causes unprecedented grounds for rejection (e.g., amendment leads to deficiency in the description or creates a new ground regarding novelty or inventive step). The new ground does not include grounds that were noticed prior to the amendment or existed without notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: adding a feature that introduces a new cited prior art requirement can generate a new ground and lead to dismissal; deletion of claims that causes deficiency in dependent claims is treated specially (may be admitted under Article 51(1) even if it causes a new ground for rejection). Examiner may refer to examples for judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner discretion on amendment requirement formalities for convenience
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding the satisfaction of amendment requirements, an examiner may make a judgment for the convenience of the examination procedure, disregarding the order of provisions in law, or the sequence of amendment matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details regarding violations of amendment requirements are found elsewhere in Part IV, Chapter 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion-generated new grounds should not automatically cause dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amendment was deletion of claims and subsequently generated a new ground for rejection (due to the deletion of claims, a dependent claim has deficiency in the description), an examiner shall not dismiss the amendment by reason aforementioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See examples (Ex3–Ex4) where deletion and re-arrangement of claims are admitted and appropriate even if they cause new issues, with examiner notifying resultant deficiencies as necessary.
